questions.q: Sleeping Beauty Castle's drawbridge has officially been lowered only ____ times.
questions.fact: Twice: on opening day in 1955 and when New Fantasyland opened in 1983.

questions.q: Sleeping Beauty Castle at Disneyland is only ____ feet tall.
questions.fact: It's 77 feet (23 m) tall. Smaller details up high make it look taller.

questions.q: Disneyland's chaotic first day in July 1955 got the nickname Black ____.
questions.fact: It was called "Black Sunday": crowds, heat, and rides breaking down.

questions.q: About half of the 28,000 people at Disneyland's 1955 opening got in with fake ____ or by climbing the fence.
questions.fact: Only about half were invited guests. The rest had counterfeit tickets or snuck over the fence.

questions.q: Disneyland has a colony of about 200 feral ____ that help keep mice away.
questions.fact: Hundreds of feral cats roam Disneyland at night and help control rodents.

questions.q: Disneyland's secret Club 33 is simply named after its ____.
questions.fact: Disney says it's named for its address: 33 Royal Street in New Orleans Square.

questions.q: When Pirates of the Caribbean opened, some of its skeletons were borrowed from ____.
questions.fact: Imagineers got real skeletons from UCLA Medical Center's anatomy department. They were later replaced.

questions.q: The Enchanted Tiki Room (1963) was the first attraction to use ____.
questions.fact: It was the first attraction to use Disney's Audio-Animatronics.

questions.q: The giant rocks in Cars Land's Cadillac Mountain Range are shaped like Cadillac ____.
questions.fact: They're shaped like Cadillac tail fins, up to 125 feet high.

questions.q: A ____ is kept burning in the window of Walt's apartment above the Main Street fire station.
questions.fact: A lamp stays lit in the window as a tribute to Walt (a little Christmas tree replaces it at the holidays).

questions.q: Pirates of the Caribbean opened in 1967, ____ months after Walt Disney died.
questions.fact: It debuted three months after his death, the last ride he helped design.

questions.q: Adventureland was first supposed to have real ____, until experts said they'd just lie around and hide.
questions.fact: Walt wanted real animals, but zoologists warned they'd hide, so Imagineers built mechanical ones.

questions.q: A group of flamingos is called a ____.
questions.fact: A flamboyance of flamingos!

questions.q: A group of crows is called a ____.
questions.fact: A murder of crows (an old-fashioned term).

questions.q: A group of owls is called a ____.
questions.fact: A parliament of owls.

questions.q: A group of porcupines is called a ____.
questions.fact: A prickle of porcupines.

questions.q: Under all that white fur, a polar bear's skin is ____.
questions.fact: Their skin, nose and lips are black, which soaks up heat.

questions.q: Butterflies taste things with their ____.
questions.fact: Taste sensors are on their feet (and mouthparts).

questions.q: An octopus has ____ hearts.
questions.fact: Three: one pumps blood around the body, two pump it through the gills.

questions.q: So they don't float away while resting, sea otters wrap themselves in ____.
questions.fact: They wrap themselves in kelp to stay put.

questions.q: Koala fingerprints are so similar to ____ fingerprints that they're hard to tell apart.
questions.fact: Koala and human fingerprints are very hard to tell apart.

questions.q: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly ____.
questions.fact: They can hover and even fly backwards.

questions.q: Wombats are the only animals known to make poop shaped like ____.
questions.fact: Wombat poop comes out as little cubes. Scientists won an Ig Nobel Prize for figuring out how.

questions.q: Before it was called the Frisbee, the flying disc was sold as the Pluto ____.
questions.fact: Walter Morrison designed the Pluto Platter in 1955 and sold it to Wham-O, which renamed it Frisbee in 1957.

questions.q: Play-Doh was first made in the 1930s as a ____.
questions.fact: It started as a putty for cleaning coal soot off wallpaper.

questions.q: Bubble Wrap was invented in 1957 by two men trying to make 3D plastic ____.
questions.fact: The wallpaper flopped, but the bubbles made great packing material.

questions.q: The Slinky was invented after an engineer saw a spring fall off a ____ and keep "walking."
questions.fact: Naval engineer Richard James saw a spring "step" down after it fell off a shelf in 1943.

questions.q: Frank Epperson's frozen-drink-on-a-stick was first called the ____.
questions.fact: He first named it the Epsicle. His kids called it "Pop's 'sicle": the Popsicle.

questions.q: In 1932, soldiers with machine guns fought a "war" in Australia against ____, and didn't win.
questions.fact: The Emu War! Lots of birds were killed, but the emu population was barely affected.

questions.q: England's first speeding fine, in 1896, was for going ____ miles per hour.
questions.fact: Walter Arnold was fined for going 8 mph in a 2 mph zone.

questions.q: Abraham Lincoln is in the National ____ Hall of Fame.
questions.fact: He was a champion wrestler as a young man, and was honored in 1992.

questions.q: Chocolate chip cookies were invented at the ____ Inn in Massachusetts.
questions.fact: Ruth Wakefield created them at her Toll House Inn in the 1930s.

questions.q: When cotton candy was introduced at the 1904 World's Fair, it was called Fairy ____.
questions.fact: It debuted as "Fairy Floss."

questions.q: Machine-made cotton candy was co-invented in 1897 by a ____.
questions.fact: Dentist William Morrison invented it with candy maker John C. Wharton.

questions.q: Hawaiian pizza (with pineapple) was invented in ____.
questions.fact: Sam Panopoulos created it in Chatham, Ontario, in 1962.

questions.q: Long ago, most carrots were ____ instead of orange.
questions.fact: Early carrots were purple or yellow. Orange carrots came later from Dutch growers.

questions.q: The man who designed the Pringles can had some of his ashes buried in a ____.
questions.fact: Fred Baur asked to have some of his ashes buried in a Pringles can.

questions.q: Nutella was created in Italy because, after the war, ____ was hard to get.
questions.fact: Cocoa was scarce, so Pietro Ferrero stretched it with hazelnuts.

questions.q: Bananas are berries, but ____ are not.
questions.fact: Botanically, bananas are berries and strawberries are not.

questions.q: Sealed honey can stay good for ____.
questions.fact: Sealed honey has an indefinite shelf life; ancient honey has been found still edible after millennia.

questions.q: In the 1830s, tomato ____ were sold as a medicine that could supposedly cure headaches and more.
questions.fact: Tomato pills were sold as cure-alls in the 1830s. Ketchup was recommended for upset stomachs too.

questions.q: When scientists tested those 1830s tomato pills, they found they contained no ____ at all.
questions.fact: The tomato pills that were analyzed didn't contain a trace of tomato!

questions.q: Walt Disney first wanted to call Mickey Mouse ____ Mouse.
questions.fact: Walt's wife Lillian talked him into "Mickey" instead.

questions.q: In early Toy Story ideas, Woody was an evil ____.
questions.fact: Woody started out as an evil ventriloquist dummy.

questions.q: Lightning McQueen's number 95 stands for the year ____ came out.
questions.fact: Toy Story, Pixar's first film, came out in 1995. His number was first going to be 57.

questions.q: Before The Lion King got its name, early drafts were called King of the ____.
questions.fact: Early treatments were titled "King of the Jungle."

questions.q: Walt Disney holds the record for winning ____ competitive Oscars, more than any person ever.
questions.fact: 22 competitive Oscars from 59 nominations (26 if you count honorary ones).

questions.q: Dumbo is one of Disney's shortest animated movies: just ____ minutes long.
questions.fact: It runs 64 minutes.

questions.q: In Up, the animators used ____ balloons in the shots of the house flying.
alt: ten thousand two hundred ninety seven
questions.fact: 10,297 balloons for flying shots, and 20,622 for the lift-off.

questions.q: Toy Story (1995) was the first movie made entirely with ____.
questions.fact: It was the first entirely computer-animated feature film.

questions.q: Mickey Mouse made his big debut in the 1928 cartoon Steamboat ____.
questions.fact: Steamboat Willie premiered November 18, 1928, in New York.

questions.q: A baby kangaroo is called a ____.
questions.fact: Baby kangaroos are joeys.

questions.q: A cow's stomach has ____ parts.
questions.fact: Four compartments help cows digest grass.

questions.q: Giraffes have ____ bones in their neck, the same as people.
questions.fact: Almost all mammals have seven neck bones. A giraffe's are just super long!

questions.q: With seahorses, the ____ give birth to the babies.
questions.fact: Male seahorses carry the eggs in a pouch and give birth.

questions.q: Gentoo penguins give their partner a ____ as a present.
questions.fact: They give smooth pebbles to their partner to help build a nest.

questions.q: Dolphins can sleep with half of their ____ awake.
questions.fact: One half of the brain rests while the other half stays alert.

questions.q: Wombats make poop shaped like ____.
questions.fact: Square poop! It helps it stay put on rocks and logs.

questions.q: Bananas count as ____ to scientists.
questions.fact: Botanically, a banana is a berry!

questions.q: An octopus has ____ hearts.
questions.fact: Three hearts and blue blood!

questions.q: Under its white fur, a polar bear has ____ skin.
questions.fact: Black skin soaks up heat from the sun.
